title: Resource profile
description: SEAM 4. results/metrics/<run_id>/resources.json - the cost half of the accuracy/memory/compute trade-off. Produced by Member 1 (benchmark.py) for every model through one code path, because a comparison table assembled from four differently-measured numbers cannot be defended. Consumed by Member 4 for Sections 4 and 6. Committed to git.

trainable_params.description: Parameters with requires_grad=True. For model_b this must be <= 100000 (assignment Section 2), which tests/test_param_budget.py asserts independently. For a partially frozen pretrained backbone this is smaller than total_params - report both in Section 5.

total_params.description: All parameters including frozen ones. This, not trainable_params, determines memory footprint at inference.

model_size_kb.description: Serialised state_dict size on disk, in kilobytes. Always stored in KB; convert to MB for the Section 5 pretrained table. Storing one unit everywhere avoids a silent KB/MB mix-up that would make the Section 6 argument wrong rather than merely imprecise.

macs.description: Multiply-accumulate operations for ONE forward pass at input_shape. Counted with thop. This is the number that shows the depthwise-separable saving in Section 2, so Model A and Model B must be counted the same way.

input_shape.description: [C, H, W] the MACs and latency were measured at. Normally [3, 64, 64]. If Member 4 runs the 128px pretrained ablation, this records it.

mean_epoch_time_s.description: Copied from history.json, not re-measured. Section 4 asks for training time per epoch.

inference_latency_ms.description: Mean milliseconds for a single-image forward pass in eval mode, after warm-up, batch size 1 - the batch size an edge device actually uses.

peak_mem_mb.description: Peak activation + parameter memory during a forward pass. The binding constraint on a microcontroller, and often the real reason a model cannot be deployed.

device.description: Hardware string, e.g. 'cpu (Intel i7-11800H)' or 'cuda:0 (RTX 3050)'. Timings are meaningless without it and Section 4 explicitly requires it. Latency for the edge argument should be measured on CPU across all models.
